checks.description: Uses ENU local frame for positioning

description: Load the public Cesium Air glb sample model and apply a CustomShader whose fragmentShaderText multiplies material.diffuse by a magenta tint sourced from a VEC3 uniform. The aircraft body should appear visibly magenta-tinted vs its default colours. Tests CustomShader uniforms, VEC3 type, and MODIFY_MATERIAL mode.
name: archive-tint-uniform-aircraft
notes: Imported from optimization/scenarios/cesiumjs-custom-shader/eval-001. Expected source/runtime contracts are scenario-authored; actual values are observed from the archived baseline generated JS and browser artifacts.

expected_behaviors: Calls Model.fromGltfAsync with the public CesiumAir glb URL
Constructs a CustomShader with uniforms: { u_tint: { type: UniformType.VEC3, value: new Cartesian3(1.0, 0.2, 0.9) } }
fragmentShaderText defines fragmentMain(FragmentInput fsInput, inout czm_modelMaterial material) and multiplies material.diffuse by u_tint
Positions the model via modelMatrix from Transforms.eastNorthUpToFixedFrame at roughly -120 long, 35 lat, 30000 m altitude
Frames the camera so the aircraft is clearly the dominant visible element
Uses minimumPixelSize and explicit camera framing so the aircraft is visible in the screenshot
preflight.landmark: CesiumAir sample model over the Pacific
preflight.visual_expectations: The Cesium Air aircraft centered and large against ocean or sky, with its fuselage and wings visibly tinted toward magenta/pink rather than the default white/blue. The aircraft silhouette should be recognizable and not clipped or off-screen. The visual assessment uses a four-shot cardinal panorama (north, east, south, west) from the settled viewer state; the subject should remain understandable across the panorama, and grading considers all screenshots together.

prompt: Load the public Cesium Air sample model from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CesiumGS/cesium/main/Apps/SampleData/models/CesiumAir/Cesium_Air.glb using Model.fromGltfAsync. Apply a CustomShader with a VEC3 uniform u_tint set to (1.0, 0.2, 0.9) (magenta) and fragmentShaderText that multiplies material.diffuse by u_tint. Position the model at -120.0 longitude, 35.0 latitude, 30000 m altitude with a Transforms.eastNorthUpToFixedFrame model matrix. Set a robust visual scale such as scale 30, minimumPixelSize 350, maximumScale 30000, and a subtle white silhouette so the aircraft is visible after load. Frame a known target point explicitly, waiting for the model to be renderable if needed, so the aircraft fills most of the screen against the ocean instead of rendering as an empty ocean/sky frame.
